description: A workshop on collective intelligence: how humans think, decide and act together. The broad event theme alone does not distinguish participants.

participants.name: Ecology researcher
participants.offers: I study the material and energy flows of computing infrastructure. I have conducted interviews with communities affected by new industrial developments and can help frame an ecological research question.
participants.needs: I want to understand how networks work inside data centres: which equipment moves information and how architecture influences physical infrastructure. I also want examples of including local knowledge in technical decisions.

participants.name: Network engineer
participants.offers: I have designed and maintained networks in computing facilities. I can explain switching, routing and redundancy with practical examples. I enjoy explaining infrastructure to non-specialists.
participants.needs: I want to understand how communities evaluate the environmental effects of data centres and which impacts engineers tend to overlook.

participants.name: Cooperative facilitator
participants.profile: I have facilitated meetings in a housing cooperative for eight years, including disputes over repairs and shared budgets. I can share practical methods for recording dissent and reaching consent. I am exploring how groups preserve minority viewpoints after making a decision, especially when membership changes.

participants.name: Deliberation researcher
participants.offers: I compare records from citizens assemblies and interview facilitators about how minority positions appear in reports. I can help analyse meeting records.
participants.needs: How do groups preserve minority viewpoints after a decision? I want to compare practical examples with research methods. I am also interested in teaching qualitative coding.

participants.name: Community artist
participants.offers: I run accessible drawing workshops and make illustrated explanations for community projects. I have experience helping people communicate ideas without specialist vocabulary.
participants.needs: I want to learn what collective intelligence means in practice. I am looking for feedback on workshop activities that make quiet participants comfortable contributing.

participants.name: Software developer
participants.offers: I build collaborative editing tools and have worked on offline synchronisation. I can explain technical trade-offs in recording group work.
participants.needs: I want concrete examples of how groups track dissent so I can design a small tool. I also need help making technical diagrams more accessible.

participants.name: Volunteer gardener
participants.profile: I organise a neighbourhood garden with rotating volunteers. We have learned how to hand over seasonal knowledge through demonstrations rather than manuals. I would like to understand collective intelligence and talk about public participation, but do not yet have a particular project in mind.

participants.name: Oral historian
participants.offers: I record oral histories and organise community archives. I can help design interviews and think about whose knowledge a formal record leaves out.
participants.needs: How can volunteer groups keep practical knowledge when members leave? I want examples of teaching through demonstration rather than relying on written documentation.
